items.title: Louis Hayes interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: His name was Clarence Stamps. But he didn’t. And he started teaching me. And I learned a lot from him.

ctx.x: Yes it really was. My father played piano and drums, and my mother played piano. And I started out playing piano, actually started out with playing piano. Most kids started out playing — because the piano is in the homes mostly. So I did that for a while. But the piano to me was, at five or six, it wasn’t fun. I think doing anything, if it’s too complicated or not fun, and someone has to more or less as a job make you do it, that causes a problem. And piano causes me a problem. But drums were there in the house…

were having doing certain things, and I looked at them and it was easy for me. So that made me, I felt good about that, because I could accomplish things real fast that they were having a lot of problems with. And then I had a — had, now he’s passed away — a cousin, that he played drums very well. He didn’t come to New York. If he’d a came to New York in the 40’s he would have been very well known. His name was Clarence Stamps. But he didn’t. And he started teaching me. And I learned a lot from him. That’s how I…
Yeah. Was there a point, let’s say in high school, that you decided that you were going to be a musician, for a living?
